This is not specified in the OGraf definition as of now. Perhaps we should add a case for when the data is badly invalid according to the schema?

Things to consider:

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: In my opinion the whole idea of the schema inside the manifest is to allow a client to present appropriate controls to the user, so that it's not possible to send invalid data to the template. I would not enforce that on the server a second time. - But I am open to other ideas.

Documentation could probably be updated with this clarification, I'll leave this issue open for someone to pick up to do just that.

title: Add support for HDR Graphics using CICP and SMPTE ST 2094-50
author: digitaltvguy
body:
1.  SMPTE ST 2094-50 adds HDR Reference white metadata and parameterized adaptive tone mapping math with a relative color space for compositing of different image formats in a single render space which is anchored to HDR Reference White luminance. SMPTE ST 2094-50 has moved past the comment stage in Public Committee Draft # 2 and moving forward to a full standard if all goes well.    

- HDR Reference White Luminance Metadata provides a common way of anchoring all elements together in a single output space
- Parameterized tone mapper separates areas above HDR Reference white which is described as (HDR) Headroom.  This is the area that typically gets compressed when mapping HDR to SDR.

2. Support PNG 3rd Edition CICP Chunk to explicitly identify image format
3. Support ICC CICP Tag to explicitly identify image format

CICP is ITU-T H.273 and identifies:

- Image primaries
- Transfer Function
- Matrix Coefficients (conversion <> between RGB and other triplets like YCbCr
- Signal Range (Full or Limited)

comments.author: dvdeurse
comments.body: Hi Chris, what is exactly the request? Support for any image format, color spaces, etc. depends on the renderer implementation and the capabilities of HTML5. OGraf should stay independent from that and should work with any of these and future technologies. So the only place where this can be relevant is to add notion of these technologies inside the `renderRequirements` of the OGraf manifest and the `renderCharacteristics` provided in the description of a Renderer inside the OGraf Server API. Is that the request/proposal or do you mean something else?

comments.author: dvdeurse
comments.body:
Notes from the Working Group meeting 2026-09-30:

We decided that these are characteristics are out of scope of the OGraf definition. We should probably better document that OGraf is not a rendering system. In the future, we might add some HDR-related fields in `renderRequirements`, but we decided to keep that in the vendor-specific space at the moment.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: See also #98

title: Outro duration
author: imaretic
body:
When using OGrafs in an NLE, it's important for the NLE to know how long a graphic takes to animate out. This ensures the graphic animates out precisely at the end of its timeline piece, for example, rendering the final frame of the outro on the last frame of the OGraf piece on the timeline.

Since a graphic can be in different states during playback, the stop duration may not always be the same.

Potential solution to this problem could be making the outro duration a function in the web component rather than a static property in the manifest file. The OGraf client could then, after setting scheduled actions, call method like `getOutroDuration()`, or the outro duration could be returned as part of the response to `setActionsSchedule()`.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
After today's (2025-10-29) discussion I try to summarize what I think would make sense in my opinion.

Add a property to the manifest with the duration of the outro animation (stopAction) in milliseconds and let it be -1 if it's unknown and varies that much, that it does not make sense to default it to anything (what should seldom be the case).

`outroDuration: 500,`

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Notes from Working Group meeting 2025-10-29:

We think that this is not limited to outros, as the animation between steps or other actions might be useful to know.
It is also relevant both for realtime and non-realtime applications.

We propose that a definition is added to the manifest that describes animation-times for different types of steps (such as intro/play, steps & outro/stop). If the animation time for a certain step is dynamic/unknown, it can be defined as "-1".
It is not a perfect solution, but having a statically defined animation-time allows for NLE's and automation software to predictably adjust action times.

comments.author: didikunz
dvdeurse
comments.body: Yes, and for the `playAction`, we probably need an optional `step` field, as every step could potentially have a different transition duration.

comments.author: didikunz
mrfanny
comments.body:
Hi,

I'm testing OGraf support in DaVinci Resolve 21 (public beta, released April 2026) and running into the exact issue described here.

DR 21 appears to call stopAction() at the very last frame of the clip, which leaves no time for the out animation to play. The in animation (playAction) works correctly.

A few questions:

Is there any known workaround that works specifically with DaVinci Resolve 21's OGraf renderer?
Has Blackmagic Design been in contact with the OGraf working group about this? Do they plan to implement outDuration or getOutroDuration() in their renderer?
Is the v_ vendor prefix approach viable as a short-term workaround — e.g. adding "v_outDuration": 900 to the manifest and hoping DR reads it?
Does setActionsSchedule get called by DR's renderer at all? In my testing I cannot confirm whether DR calls it or just calls playAction + stopAction directly.
For context: I'm building a lower-third name graphic (similar to the l3rd-name example in this repo). Everything works except the out animation.

Thanks

title: ServerApi: Propsal/clarification: prefix in URL
author: nytamin
body:
I'd like to be able to implement an Ograf Server which exposes its OGraf API on urls with various prefixes.
For example, the API can be exposed on url `johans-server.com/myPrefix/MyFolder/something-else/ograf/v1/**`.

I'd like to hear your thoughts on this, and whether we should modify the API specification to explicitly support this?
eg, `/graphics` -> `{prefix}/graphics`.
Or is this implied to be acceptable already? (I'm a bit unsure what the OpenAPI spec allows and not.)

Another question to consider is should we require the url to be prefixed with `/ograf/v1/**`? (this might be useful in case we'd add breaking changes in the future).

comments.author: dvdeurse
comments.body:
Reading the OpenAPI spec, what comes close to what you ask is the `servers` field (see https://learn.openapis.org/specification/servers.html). It allows you to specify a list of 'prefixes' in your OpenAPI definition. Typical use case is when you have multiple environments (like dev, staging, production) and you provide the base URL for each environment. A UI visualizing your OpenAPI spec can then easily switch between these servers. However, this solution is not feasible for the OGraf OpenAPI spec, because these prefixes are vendor-specific and can never be part of the actual OpenAPI definition in our case. So the real answer here is: is it possible to formally describe it with OpenAPI that various prefixes are allowed: no. Do we allow various prefixes: yes, but we need to explicitly mention this in plain normative text.

Regarding you proposal for adding the version inside the URL, it is a pattern that you see a lot but I'm personally not a big fan of it. The advantage of doing that, is that it is very clear for clients against which version they are talking to. The disadvantage is as follows. Implementations supporting multiple versions need to duplicate their endpoints, even if they are actually still doing exactly the same thing (I guess there will be some breaking changes, but not everything will be changed). This is needed if you want to keep supporting clients that are on older versions. If you don't introduce a version in your path, server implementations only need to implement the new things (on condition that this is possible). Besides, for the OGraf spec, we promised to keep it both backwards and forwards compatible. Why shouldn't we keep that promise for the Server API?

comments.author: rinode
comments.body:
> Besides, for the OGraf spec, we promised to keep it both backwards and forwards compatible. Why shouldn't we keep that promise for the Server API

I think this should be formalized if that's the case, as it's indeed very common to have API versioning in REST APIs. Guaranteeing bidirectional compatibility can elimitate the need for this... but it could become a maintenance burden down the road.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Notes from Working Group 2026-03-18:

Yes, this should be allowed, let's update the specification to clarify that it is.

title: Suggestion: real-time transport mode (AsyncApi?)
author: rinode
body:
Just to provide some extra context and avoid misunderstanding: this suggestion concerns high frequency updates of graphics properties while it's on air and if OGraf should play a role here.

Last meeting got me thinking... @axelboberg raised a very interesting point about transport, whether we have ever considered using WebSockets. Generally, HTTP/3 (using QUIC, based on UDP) should provide a boost in performance over 'traditional' HTTP over TCP, with only one round-trip for the handshake and lost packets being non-blocking. However... Have we ever benchmarked this, especially for high framerate scenarios?

Should the need arise for low-latency communication, would it be an idea to adopt AsyncApi, but using the OpenApi schema? See: https://www.asyncapi.com/docs/tutorials/getting-started/coming-from-openapi, they seem quite clear about this:
> AsyncAPI is compatible with OpenAPI schemas.

Perhaps this is a nice performance profiling/benchmark task, a cross-comparison of framerates and transport modes:
- Framerates: 23.976, 25fps, 29.97fps, 30fps, 50fpx, 59.94fps, 60fps, 120fps
- Transport:  REST over HTTP/2 (TCP), REST over HTTP/3 (QUIC/UDP), WebSockets (TCP), WebTransport (HTTP/3)

Would love to hear your input! Let's get technical 🤓

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
I don't know, if there is a misunderstanding, what the whole thing is about. The Server-API is used to control the play-out of graphic templates. 

I don't know, if you are familiar with [CasparCG](https://casparcg.com/) There is the [AMCP-protocol](https://github.com/CasparCG/help/wiki/AMCP-Protocol) that does something similar. It's based on TCP-IP socket communication. You use it to tell the server, what and when you want to play something. You do not call it frame by frame. As the HTML-template itself usually needs a short time to load itself, that would not make sense. The idea is, that an operator loads a template (lower third etc.) a few seconds before it needs to go on air, and then plays it on cue. The communication latency is the least problem here. But usually this works quite well and timing is seldom an issue.

comments.author: axelboberg
comments.body:
What you're saying @didikunz is true for simple graphics such as nameplates and titles. However whenever something needs to be updated on a frame-by-frame basis this starts becoming more interesting.

Some examples:
- A template rendering a clock from an external input such as a sports event
- Multiple redundant servers that need to depend on an external state
- Templates relying on positional data from external sources

Sure you can still do this with AMCP but then you'd have to abandon the standard. And even though you may have a faster transport the load command is still relevant.

comments.author: rinode
comments.body:
I guess it comes down to whether those properties are controllable from an OGraph perspective, or should be considered "internally controlled" and not exposed through the protocol. It does raise questions about what the real-time mode in the OGraph spec actually entails – and more importantly: what not.

Regarding the misunderstanding @didikunz: this is exactly the answer I gave @axelboberg regarding the "purpose" of the Server API last meeting. But it doesn't completely rule it out.

In the end, if the API is not built for this, it might be good if we advise against this in its documentation.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
I am not completely against it, but most of the mentioned stuff is not done via the server API. For instance a clock is usually done with some internal logic, that either count on it's own, use the system clock or connect to a timing source directly. 

For stuff like football or basketball the latency of these protocols are usually fast enough to set the game clock (or shot clock) from the server. For instance the [ScoreboardOCR](https://scoreboard-ocr.com/) app does exactly this (not yet for OGraf).

comments.author: rinode
comments.body:
For example, let's take this graphic that @nytamin shared:
https://github.com/ebu/ograf/issues/47

If the positions of those labels were to be provided by an external tracking system, sending updates every frame while the graphic is on-air... Would we say that's out of scope for OGraf and should be handled internally by the playout system itself? Or do we perhaps want to explore the possibilities and limitations here?

comments.author: axelboberg
comments.body:
That is a good example. The question whether or not this is in scope of OGraf requires more knowledge of the intentions of the protocol than I currently have.

My initial thoughts however, and seeing this as a way to standardize how graphics templates are controlled both in live settings and offline (non real time), is that I fear lacking a good real time transport would force developers out of the standard for way too little or no reason.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
This is a quite interesting idea!
There was an intention when designing the OGraf API to make it versatile enough so most vendors wouldn't have to resort to secondary data channels when implementing their graphics in OGraf (that's why we included the "v_" prefix, for vendor-specific extensions of the API).

I can see a few possible options:

* Discard the REST API entirely, in favor of a websocket one _(a _very_ breaking change. Still allowed at this point, but would require much work and likely delay the release of the Server API)._
* Keep the REST API, but also add a functionally equivalent one based on websockets (AsyncApi based on the same OpenApi schema). _(A lot of work, but could be added in a later version)_
* Add a SINGLE websocket API endpoint for the "update" method only (since that will likely be the one most commonly used for realtime updates). _(Least amount of extra work)_

---

Just out of curiosity; to see if a REST API implementation can be capable of handling realtime data updates I ran a quick test locally using [OGraf Server](https://github.com/SuperFlyTV/ograf-server), pushing data updates at 60 fps to a local renderer and filmed it in slow-motion:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c3a6fc4-731d-4fae-a103-10c7d5e85af9

It looks like _most__ of the data comes through in time for each frame to get updated, so that's pretty good.
The calls took about 3-5ms, and that includes a roundtrip of the message being passed from Controller to Server to Renderer and back again.
But this was a local test, perhaps network overhead would be higher over a typical network..

comments.author: rinode
comments.body:
Certainly not an easy choice.

Discarding the REST API feels radical, but I would prefer that over maintaining two API's if we treat this as a priority. I do fear that it might affect the adoption of OGraf though.

We were developing a combined OpenAPI / AsyncAPI protocol when I worked at EVS (for Cerebrum), I'll check in with them to see how that's working out. It might help us to decide whether it's worth going down that road. I do recall some of your colleagues at SuperFly implementing that protocol @nytamin, would be good to hear about their experiences.

comments.author: dvdeurse
comments.body:
Interesting discussion, but let's not forget our audience and Tuomo's infamous 80-20 rule. Why do we specify a schema for each parameter? Because implementers of controllers can then render them without prior knowledge. Why do you want to render them? So users can control it. In most of the cases, updating graphics will be triggered by manual interaction. Does that mean we prevent automated updates? Of course not. Most of the automated updates will not be every frame either, on the contrary. So I want to highlight that this case is relevant, but is only about a small portion of everyday's graphics updates.

Let's focus on these high-frequency update use cases. I see two categories:
* fully automated, no user interaction at all: the clock example falls in this category, as well as an algorithm that tracks players on a pitch and provides the bounding boxes. So for these use cases, what is the benefit to create an OGraf parameter for this? You will never have to visualize it in a controller. The only thing I see is that you expose a consistent way for external systems to 'push' this data into the template. But should we use (or misuse?) OGraf for that? You could easily build and define your own API (in whatever technology) and use it inside your template, you would obtain the same consistency. 
* user-driven: for example a user manipulating a (physical or virtual) joystick, a T-bar, a jog to steer certain parameter values. You could still tackle this in the same way as the previous point (i.e. build an API where these controls are talking to and push them into your graphics via your preferred transport). However, I see more reasons that this category could benefit from being a parameter because it is possible to show them in the controller and to interact with it as a user. A noticeable difference here is that the interaction is not full time, but only when the user actually does something. However, when the user does something, it generate high-frequency updates.

So in my opinion, only user-driven high-frequency updates are valid use cases for this topic. That said, what are the options if we want to render based on high-frequency updates:
1) not make it a parameter at all, and implement the communication channel inside the template implementation. This solution will work in every compliant renderer and what's more, the implementer can choose the best protocol that suite his/her needs. You have access to all the options available and are not restricted to what the OGraf spec supports today (whatever that may be).
2) introduce a WebSocket endpoint for updates only (and I assume we keep the one in the REST API as well). A valid proposal although annoying for vendors that don't need this feature. You could make it optional but many optional things inside a spec is not great for the overall interoperability. We should think about whether it is worth to annoy the 80% in order to please the 20% :-). 

For me the other options like fully replacing the API with an Async API or maintaining two APIs would be enormous overkill and a bad signal towards the vendors that focus on the 'simple' use cases.

comments.author: rinode
comments.body:
> Why do we specify a schema for each parameter? Because implementers of controllers can then render them without prior knowledge. Why do you want to render them? So users can control it.

I think it all boils down to whether this is indeed the focus, as you could also treat it as an abstraction layer for graphics control where you don't care whether it's controlled by a human, or automated and at what frequency. We did a show once where the position of a graphic was based upon multi-touch dragging on a touchscreen: high-frequency, user-driven, but causing a massive burst of updates that you probably don't want to wire through OGraf.

It would be good to formalize the intent of the protocol, to prevent anyone treating it like such an abstraction layer and building full-blown automated data connection workflows on top of it, if it's simply not built for it.

Just because you can, doesn't mean you should 😊

comments.author: dvdeurse
comments.body:
Well, the use case does make sense, and can even be done with HTTP as Johan demonstrated. Since this was a local test, I assume this was HTTP 1.1? From HTTP2 and further, things can only get better in this context :). So we shouldn't prevent or discourage users from doing this, if it fits their requirements, why not. But I agree that for users that need to go beyond the boundaries of static HTTP requests, we can (and should) provide guidelines if we decide not to introduce an OGraf WebSocket endpoint.

I don't think this is about 'intents', but about how to achieve interoperability across multiple vendors without ruling out certain use cases, but at the same time make adoption as easy as possible.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: Interesting points. I second Tuomo's 80/20 rule: Keep the basics as simple as possible. Another thing maybe worth considering is, that we should keep the template authoring process for basic stuff as simple as possible, so that basic web-developers (or automated tools) can quickly and easily create OGraf templates. While the uses cases, that you mention are usually handled by high skilled programmers who even dream in JavaScript :)

comments.author: rinode
comments.body: For the sake of familiarization I'll look into a very "simple" benchmark (it never really is simple!), exploring the boundaries of HTTP version (1.1/2/3) vs. update frequency (framerates for now) vs. payload size (one property, five properties, ten properties... fifty??) using OGraf. That could give us some numbers that might help in deciding whether this is worth further investigating. While I am leaning more and more towards prioritizing the simplicity of the protocol, it's still worth measuring!

comments.author: axelboberg
comments.body:
> This is a quite interesting idea! There was an intention when designing the OGraf API to make it versatile enough so most vendors wouldn't have to resort to secondary data channels when implementing their graphics in OGraf (that's why we included the "v_" prefix, for vendor-specific extensions of the API).
> 
> I can see a few possible options:
> 
> * Discard the REST API entirely, in favor of a websocket one _(a _very_ breaking change. Still allowed at this point, but would require much work and likely delay the release of the Server API)._
> * Keep the REST API, but also add a functionally equivalent one based on websockets (AsyncApi based on the same OpenApi schema). _(A lot of work, but could be added in a later version)_
> * Add a SINGLE websocket API endpoint for the "update" method only (since that will likely be the one most commonly used for realtime updates). _(Least amount of extra work)_
> 
> Just out of curiosity; to see if a REST API implementation can be capable of handling realtime data updates I ran a quick test locally using [OGraf Server](https://github.com/SuperFlyTV/ograf-server), pushing data updates at 60 fps to a local renderer and filmed it in slow-motion:
> 
>  VID_20260305_210047616.mp4 
> 
> It looks like _most__ of the data comes through in time for each frame to get updated, so that's pretty good. The calls took about 3-5ms, and that includes a roundtrip of the message being passed from Controller to Server to Renderer and back again. But this was a local test, perhaps network overhead would be higher over a typical network..

I'll just jump in and mention that while this is a good test for speeds on a local network it doesn't take request ordering into account, so it implies that logic for handling dropped or late data is required to be implemented within templates. Whereas another transport would solve that issue.

I hear what you're saying about 80/20, I just can't help wondering if playout commands in real time settings at least shouldn't be limited by HTTP requests. Maybe I'm wrong.

comments.author: rinode
comments.body:
> it doesn't take request ordering into account, so it implies that logic for handling dropped or late data is required to be implemented within templates.

Yep... This touches the whole aspect of frame accuracy with HTML Graphics though. I completely agree that for simple use-cases (still the majority and from what I gather the focus of OGraf) the current approach works. But I would be careful with basing our verdict on high-frequency updates on one demo, where only one property is updated at high frequency on a local network. That's a very favorable scenario.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: As suggested elsewhere: Maybe a "Profile" approach, similar to the ones in MOS, could be the solution, so that a real time protocol could be specified as a separate profile. The schema would then need to have a way to indicate that the template need this functionality.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Note from Working Group 2026-04-15:

Not that many opinions where raised.
The 80/20 rule probably applies, so we probably don't want to replace the whole REST API with an AsyncAPI.
But we recognize the usefulness of having a higher performance API in some cases.

No conclusion reached, discussion to be continued next meeting.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Notes from the Working Group meeting 2026-04-29:

There was a question whether we have a real-world use case that highlights the need for a high-performance API (and that the REST API is not performant enough)?
We concluded that we'll stick to the REST API for now, as we think that will be easier to use for the most common use cases.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body: I'll close this thread for now. If anyone want to champion this at a later time and can present a strong use case we'll reopen it.

title: Question: non-linear graphic steps
author: rinode
body: So the [step model](https://github.com/ebu/ograf/blob/main/v1/specification/docs/Specification.md) is visualized as a linear path: However, the documentation doesn't specifically mention whether a step is meant to be linear (i.e. a 'marker' on a timeline), or can be non-linear, such as the following example: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8cd02e1-ff41-4f3d-aece-732473c5437e) In this example, directionality of transitions affects the step it will traverse. Another example: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0beb0172-9cef-4815-be4c-10187353cc3d) Is OGraf's step model restricted to linear timelines, or can steps diverge to (and join from) separate paths?

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
As I understand it, the step model is more in a linera fashion. What you show here can be represented with custom commands.
Call "step 1" then either "A", "B" or "C" and then "step 2". While the steps would maybe not be called "step X".

comments.author: rinode
dvdeurse
comments.body:
The step model does not have to be linear. I don't think OGraf should have an opinion about what steps mean. It is the implementer of the Graphics that determines the semantics of the steps for that Graphics. All OGraf defines is 
* the fact that a Graphic can have multiple steps
* a step is identified by a number
* a function to navigate to these steps (either absolute or relative). 

What this actually means (i.e. rendering a particular step) is up to the Graphics implementer and can depend on internal state, external state, step number, etc. And yes, you could use custom actions to manipulate the current step, if that is necessary, but it shouldn't be a requirement to implement non-linear step models.

comments.author: christianeide
comments.body:
I agree that the step model should not be locked to a linear, I have several usecases where a non-linear step model makes sense. F. ex. if you have several images in a full screen or studio screen, then we would like to jump to whatever image the user wants.

With that being said, from my own experience it is more demanding to create graphics that handles non-linear playout. So I dont think Ograf should demand that everyone should support non-linear step logic. And at the same time not limit users to only support a linear step logic.

Should this be a configuration the graphic instance declears? If the graphics can handle non-linear, or orderLocked, step?

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
The OGraf specification actually supports a non linear way of the stepCount. That is correct. If that makes sense or not is not the point. Actually you can either use the stepCount or could use a customAction. That depends on the use case, while you only could give the stepCount (a number) as a parameter in the first case you can send a full payload with data (variables etc.) in the second case. 

By the way: I would do the use-case of the studio screen you mentioned by updating the image and not by loading everything beforehand and step back and fore. But it sure could be done that way if it makes sense for any reason.

comments.author: rinode
comments.body: Going from a step to a directly connected step feels natural, but with diverging/joining paths and being able to select 'multiple steps ahead' complexity arises (multiple possible paths to the same step). Then again, why would you introduce diverging paths if you don't explicitly want to traverse them... I'm not big on introducing another mode, but if we want to fully support this it might be good to provide the necessary feedback to determine which steps can be taken.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
Hmmm. I think there is a slight misunderstanding here. The diagrams are meant to show possible ways to call these steps, not the way they must be called. 

In CasparCG we have the "Next" command, that works similar, but in a less flexible way. It simply calles the next step, without giving the operator a way to skip steps. In my understanding the nextStep variable is more to be able to skip steps to preview a step before putting it on air, similar to the "skipAnimation" flag. Mostly this step animations are used to either show other pages of informations (like for a ranking in sports) or to reveal something, like having a bars showing the points/percentages in a voting and revealing the actual names of the winners one by one. In such scenarios it can be handy to be able to skip to a step to see it as preview but would ruin the tension if used on air.

So I would keep this stuff as simple as possible and not over engineer it too much. But that is only my opinion.

comments.author: rinode
comments.body: It feels like we've reached consensus about this: steps can be non-linear, but step transitions are unopinionated and left to the implementer to handle correctly.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Notes from Working Group meeting 2026-04-29:

Yes, we agree with @rinode 's comment above.

title: ServerApi: Something to load data into a store
author: didikunz
body:
In CasparCG there are commands (DATA STORE, DATA RETRIEVE, DATA LIST, DATA REMOVE) that allows to send template data to a storage under a name. The template play-out commands allow this name be given instead of the (JSON or XML) data for the template. This is often used, when some external data is processed by a middle ware (stock courses etc.) and simply are sent to a data-set on the server. I think that this should be a vendor-specific implementation (ie not added to the ograf-specification) for now. If it turns out that there is a massive need for this, we could add it as a opt-in feature in a later version.

title: Rendering engine version
author: imaretic
body:
Despite OGrafs being defined by this specification, they can still render differently across different “OGraf renderers” since not every “OGraf renderer” will be using the same version of HTML rendering engine (Blink, Gecko, etc.), where differences in support for specific HTML, CSS, or JS features can occur. It would be useful to include the minimum compatible engine version for the template in the manifest file because the choice of rendering engine directly affects how OGrafs are displayed. This requirement could potentially be added to the `RenderRequirement` object of the manifest file.

Since CEF is commonly used in video production software, we should consider whether it makes sense to specify minimum CEF version requirements only, or whether the manifest should remain flexible enough to support defining minimum versions for other rendering engines as well.

title: Schema property order
author: imaretic
body:
Schema properties in OGraf manifest are contained within the `schema` JSON object, which means there is no defined order in which the controller UI will read and render input elements to the user.

This can be inconvenient, as less important (or optional) properties may appear before more important ones, making the interface harder to use.

A potential solution to this problem could be to add an optional `order` property to each schema property item.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: That's a good point. Another solution could be to just let the UI render the controls from top to bottom, let the order in which the properties are listed be the implicit order number. AFAIK that is also the way it's meant to be in GDD.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
I think this would be a good addition. To further add to the context, the order of properties in a json-object is implied only, and not guaranteed to be unchanged.

>"An object is an unordered collection of zero or more name/value pairs, where a name is a string and a value is a string, number, boolean, null, object, or array." (Source [RFC 7159](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7159))

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Notes from Working Group meeting 2025-10-29:

Conclusion: Let's add an optional `order` property

title: Suggestion: "group" property in manifest
author: jhobz
body:
Oftentimes multiple graphics are meant to share the same area of the output, e.g. a lower-third, or a full screen takeover. If we add a top-level "group" property (string) to the manifest file, renderers could use this to compare against any graphics that are currently playing and play their stop action whenever a new graphic is played into that group.

For example, if I have a ticker at the bottom of the screen and want to play a different graphic to bring up a call-to-action in the same screen space, I'd define the group for both graphics to be "footer" (or similar). When I run the `playAction` for the CTA, the renderer automatically calls `stopAction` on all graphics in the "footer" group then, after the promise returns, runs the `playAction` for the CTA graphic.

While I think the benefits to this solution are rather evident, I can already see some drawbacks:
* The server would now need to keep track of state of which graphics are in/out -- note, not which are _loaded_, but which are currently _playing_ -- which is a non-trivial additional complexity.
* This proposal would mean the play action would not happen immediately after issuing the command from a controller, it would happen after the return of the `stopAction` promises from other graphics in the group. This is likely what the user would want in most cases, but it still means there would be no way to force the `playAction` to happen instantly.

Perhaps a better implementation would be adding an optional parameter in the `playAction` API call to tell the server to pay attention to the group property? Or make the group property an object rather than a string, with a shape similar to below?
```json
"group": {
    "name": "footer"
    "simultaneousGraphicsAllowed": 1
}
```

Interested in thoughts from others. I know in my own implementations this is already a parameter I've been looking for.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
My intention is to keep the OGraf standard as slim and simple as possible, and because of that, I would not want to add this. 

I have this situation with one client. Durring their news program the always show a graphic with the Theme for the whole story. This occupies the area, where the lower third is shown. So to make that work, I use a JavaScript feature called "Local Storage". It allows to write and read values to a storage, that can be accessed by all browser windows. The trick here is, that the other templates can subscribe to an event, that always occur, when something is written to the storage. So the lower third templates make the theme disappear and, on animating out let it reappear. This is quite an easy workflow and is only used when necessary.

comments.author: dvdeurse
comments.body:
What you ask is I think related to a concept we introduced in the Server API (https://ograf.ebu.io/v1/specification/open-api/docs/index.html): `RenderTarget`. It is a concept introduced to support layers and more advanced forms of grouping inside a rendering engine. The idea is to not restrict implementers of rendering engines to a one-dimensional layer structure, but that they are free to define their own structure, which we call with a more generic name 'RenderTarget'. So that group you are referring to can be seen as a RenderTarget. Note that it is up to the implementer how a RenderTarget is interpreted:
* implementer defines the schema
* implementer decides how many graphics are allowed per RenderTarget
* implementer decides how RenderTarget 'conflicts' are resolved (e.g. smooth crossfade transition or just a cut, or something else).

Now, from a manifest perspective, there is currently no notion of a default RenderTarget for a given graphic. And that is normal, because a RenderTarget is specific for the renderer, not the graphic itself. I can imagine that there will be vendor specific fields in the manifest allowing you to specify a default render target. Inside LiveOS, we do that as well. But I think it is hard to specify such a thing from an OGraf perspective.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Notes from Working Group meeting 2026-03-18:

This seems like a useful thing to add, but _at this time_ we're not able to come up with a definition that would both be generic and useable by a Controller.

So we'll close this thread as **Not Planned** for now, but we'll keep the door open in case someone comes up with a solution in the future.

title: Suggestion: GDD graphics positions
author: nytamin

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: Do we really need an extra specification for this? To me it simply looks like an array of numbers/integers.

comments.author: dvdeurse
comments.body:
Agreed, that is my feeling as well. It is a dangerous path to introduce these kind of parameter types, because you don't know where this ends. They are useful, but what is our incentive to make this particular (extension) type part of the spec and others not. 

The only advantage you achieve is a potential nicer representation of this kind of data across different vendor-specific controllers. Suppose we don't standardize these types, but a specific vendor wants to use this, am I right that the vendor can extend the OGraf schema with new types that are only known in the vendor's ecosystem?

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
>Do we really need an extra specification for this? To me it simply looks like an array of numbers/integers.

Yes, the underlying data structure is JSON, as is all the GDD types. My intention with this proposal is I think that it would be useful for GUI:s to know about positions-type data, so that they can provide better user interfaces.


>The only advantage you achieve is a potential nicer representation of this kind of data across different vendor-specific controllers.

Agreed, but that also apply to all GDD-types. They allow for a GUI to provide a nicer GUI for both simple and complex json data types.

> what is our incentive to make this particular (extension) type part of the spec and others not.

As the original creator of GDD, it was my intention that they would be extended with new types continously, to provide a better user experience.
The GDD-types are all designed to be opt-in and to [allow for graceful degradation](https://github.com/ebu/ograf/tree/main/v1/specification/json-schemas/gdd#gdd-types), ie fall back to primitive data types if a particular GUI can't render a particular GDD-type.

The GDD-types are all designed to be opt-in and to [allow for graceful degradation](https://github.com/ebu/ograf/tree/main/v1/specification/json-schemas/gdd#gdd-types), ie fall back to primitive data types if a particular GUI can't render a particular GDD-type.

title: PSA: Moving of GDD info Ograf
author: nytamin
body:
## TLDR;

GDD will be adopted by Ograf and eventually deprecated.

## Background

[GDD (Graphics Data Definition)](https://github.com/SuperFlyTV/GraphicsDataDefinition) is a json-schema data definition for CasparCG Graphics, created by Superfly.tv in 2022.

It is referenced from the ograf specification, used for defining rich data input types.

## Discussion

As brought up in #5 and later discussed in the Working Group, if would fit the ograf project well to adopt the GDD rich data inputs definitions, and maintain those discussions.

SuperFly.tv, via Johan Nyman (@nytamin) is open to the idea of moving the GDD definitions and eventually deprecating them in favor of ograf.

title: Clarify Web component interface
author: dvdeurse
body:
The first implementations of OGrafs from the field showed some similar 'bugs' across implementors, meaning that we could improve our explanation in the specification, potentially with examples to make things more tangible. Issues I've seen:
- `currentStep` was not provided in the response of the `playAction()` function. Or when provided, it was unclear that the steps were zero-index based.
- the `load()` function returns a promise that only must resolve when the graphic is fully loaded and can process a `playAction()`. In a couple of cases, the promise was resolved almost immediately without properly waiting for the full initialization of the graphic. 
- the `data` param in the `load()` function was ignored.
- the`skipAnimation` param in `playAction()` and `stopAction()` functions was ignored.

title: Caution about AdditionalProperties = False
author: adam-gol
body: `v1/specification/json-schemas/graphics/schema.json` limits "additional properties" which restricts expansion and user-extensions.  May want to reconsider why additional properties need to be restricted.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Thanks for your input!

I added the AdditionalProperties=false to the schemas in order to enforce the clause about "Vendor specific fields": https://ograf.ebu.io/v1/specification/docs/Specification#vendor-specific-fields

>Vendor-specific fields are additional fields that are not part of this specification, but used for vendor-specific means. They can occur in the Manifest file or in the payload of the requests/responses for each of the functions in the Web Component. Every vendor-specific field MUST use the prefix v_. For example, v_editor is a valid vendor-specific field, editor is not a valid field.

By combining the AdditionalProperties=false and `"patternProperties": { "^v_.*": {}}`, other properties are allowed, but only if they are prefixes with "v_".

For context, we added the clause on vendor specific fields to the specification to ensure forwards compatibility, as it allows us to add properties in the future without the risk of clashing with any preexisting, vendor specific properties.

title: Step model vs updateAction
author: didikunz
body:
Concerning the manifest: While we have a way to tell a controller, that we can have multiple steps, using the step-model of the playAction, we have no way to tell the controller, that the template expects multiple updates to show more data. For instance a ranking in sports may have 10 lines, that show rank 1 to 10 on the first play. To advance to the next page the controller would send an update for rank 11 to 20 and so on. I think it would maybe make sense to have a setting in the manifest, that explains this in a way.

For instance a boolean called "multipage" or so. Maybe somebody has a better idea than that.

For example, _in my graphics_, I often send the full list as well as a `page: number` property, so a "multipage" with a pre-specified functionality wouldn't work for me.

title: Proposal: Change the manifest file name to "*.ograf.json"
author: nytamin
body:
This is a follow-up from https://github.com/ebu/ograf/pull/10

When we changed the file name of manifest files to "*.ograf" if had the consequence that text editors doesn't automatically pick up that the file is a json-file.

This causes a useability issue, since graphics developers that uses a text-editor with json-schema support (like VSCode) won't get the intellisense automatically.
Of course, VSCode can be manually configured to accept all *.ograf files as json, but not it being done automatically is a drawback, I think.

Therefore, I propose that we modify the specification to require manifest files to be "*.ograf.json" instead of "*.ograf".

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body:
I think that the small lack of usability does not out weight the gain on simplicity for client programmers and the like. In fact the lack of automatic support can also be a plus, as inexperienced users are scared away by a file extension they don't know, instead of starting to fumble around with something they should not. To them it looks much more important, when it's called .ograf. 

What do you all think?

comments.author: Dan-Shields
comments.body: If the file is intended to always be functionally JSON, I'd be strongly against a new file extension for the sake of it. I've seen other projects use the `<name>.<scope>.json` format with no problems. To me new file extensions should be used when a new format is actually being specced, not just to signal importance. That's what good documentation is for.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Notes from Working Group meeting 2025-07-02:

Conclusion: Yes, let's change it to ".ograf.json"

title: Preview
author: PeterNicos
body:
Does Ograf define a way to realise a preview?
I was thinking of something like a preview state, that could be used for:
- a previewchannel before a graphic template is played out live
- views of many graphics for example in an ograf explorer to have a visual representation of the graphic in addition to e.g. the filename

That previewstate would not have to be connected to any other state but would be very convenient for a graphics operator or as a default state when filling out graphic templates.
Have I missed it somewhere or is that something you thought of, but have left open for every vendor to solve on their own on purpose?

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
In the current draft, the ograf does not specify a specific preview state. The intention with this is to not dictate the inner workings of a graphic, but instead leave it up to vendors to implement.

There is the `skipAnimation` property, which can be used to to preview a graphic. Currently, it is only present in the playAction and stopAction, but [this PR]( https://github.com/ebu/ograf/pull/8) suggests to add it to all actions.

If you think this should change and that there should be some type of preview state, feel free to join the [Working group ](https://tech.ebu.ch/groups/html_graphics) (or write in this thread and I'll forward your suggestions at the next meeting).

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
**Notes from Working Group meeting 2025-07-02:**

There was a discussion around this, the general consensus was that we do think it is useful to be able to preview a graphic, but that it should be sufficent to use the existing `skipAnimation` property for this.

If you want to preview a graphic, you would send a `playAction({ skipAnimation: true })`, and the graphic would display the first step (or equivalent state) instantly.

title: Font handling
author: didikunz
body:
I don't know if that is the right place to contribute...

I just recently stumbled upon the [CSS Font Loading API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CSS_Font_Loading_API). As this is available in the "document" object I guess the HTML Element would not have access to it. Would it be possible to add something to the manifest, that allow to demand the loading of fonts using this API? It would then be nice, that the template would be informed, when that has been done, and when it would have a way to tell the host, when these fonts are not needed any more. I hope I made myself clear. 

This would give templates a way to kind of embed fonts into itself. like it was possible with Flash (what was one of the gratest features in my opinion).

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: Another way would be to give the template a way to access the "document" object via some API call. That would keep the manifest clean. This could be added as parameter to the Load function or as a request that the template could call.

comments.author: nytamin
didikunz
comments.body: It seems, that I still think too much in another programming language (VB.NET) to realize, that in JavaScript something can be accessed without having an explicite reference too it. Yes, if that works this way, we can close and forget this issue. Thanks for testing.

title: GDD obsolete?
author: didikunz
body: Will the [GDD metadata format](https://github.com/SuperFlyTV/GraphicsDataDefinition/issues) become obsolete in favor of ograf manifest?

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
I will bring this up for discussion at the next working group meeting. Currently OGraf uses GDD under the hood for its data schemas, my concerns are whether we should a) reference GDD from OGraf and make it clearer (especially regarding version management and backwards/forwards compatibility), or b) OGraf takes over/absorbs the GDD schemas.

My personal opinion (as the developer of GDD) is that GDD is a suboptimal specification compared to OGraf.

comments.author: didikunz
comments.body: I would also suggest giving up GDD in favor of OGraf. We need no more standards :)

title: Sample manifest files do not contain mandatory reference to JavaScript implementation
author: mtoweber
body: The main: "....." reference is present in the readme sample, but there are not references in the samples themselves.

comments.author: nytamin
comments.body:
Good spot! At one stage during the discussions, the `"main": string` property was optional, but you're correct in that it is required in the current specification draft.

I'll update the json-schema and examples to match.
